topics.label: Lecture introduction
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the opening framing and introductory context for the lecture on complement.

topics.label: Fundamentals and core biology of complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the foundational concepts, nomenclature rules, and central biochemical role of C3 in the complement cascade.

topics.label: Complement activation pathways
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the three recognition pathways and threshold mechanisms that initiate complement activation on pathogen surfaces.

topics.label: Effector mechanisms of complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the downstream effector processes executed by activated complement to eliminate pathogens and stimulate inflammation.

topics.label: Host regulation of complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the regulatory proteins and mechanisms that protect healthy host cells from complement-mediated destruction.

topics.label: Clinical complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details the distinct clinical presentations and disease phenotypes caused by deficiencies in specific complement components.

topics.label: Pathogen evasion of complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explores how microbial pathogens have evolved specialized strategies to circumvent complement-mediated immune destruction.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the closing framing and remarks on the next topic in the lecture series.
